title: Part 4 — ReactJS
tagline: React 19 with Vite 8 and React Router 8, following F8's videos without the tooling drifting.
intro: F8's React course dates from 2022 and uses Create React App, now unmaintained. The ideas still hold; this page shows how to do the same with October 2026 tools.
Start only once part 3's checklist is done. Nine times out of ten, a strange React bug is a JavaScript bug.

blocks.caption: From an empty project to a TikTok clone.

items.label: Create a project with Vite
items.detail: One command makes a working React project that reloads on save
explain: npm create vite@latest asks for a name and a template; pick React and JavaScript. npm run dev serves it at localhost:5173.
Vite replaces the video's Create React App: it starts fast, reloads instantly, and is the first tool react.dev lists for building a React app from scratch.

items.label: Components & JSX
items.detail: Each piece of interface is a function returning JSX, assembled into a page
explain: JSX looks like HTML but is JavaScript: className instead of class, {price} inserts a variable, and each component returns exactly one root.
Component names start with a capital, like ProductCard; lowercase names are read as HTML tags.

items.label: Props & state
items.detail: Props come down from the parent; state is data the component holds and changes
explain: useState returns [value, setter]. Calling the setter makes React redraw; assigning the variable directly changes nothing on screen.
Change arrays or objects in state with a new copy: setTodos([...todos, newTodo]), never todos.push.

items.label: useEffect for APIs
items.detail: Run side work after drawing: call APIs, set timers, listen to window events
explain: The dependency array decides when it reruns: [] runs once on mount, [userId] reruns whenever userId changes.
In development, StrictMode runs effects twice to expose missing cleanup. Seeing an API called twice in dev is normal.

items.label: React Router 8
items.detail: Many pages in one app, changing the URL without a reload
explain: Install react-router (version 8). The video uses react-router-dom 6, but BrowserRouter, Routes, Route, Link and useParams are written the same; only the import changes.
Route path="/products/:id" matches any /products/42; useParams() returns { id: '42' }.

items.label: The TikTok project
items.detail: Build the layout, a header with API search, and a sidebar, with F8's videos
explain: Build it with Vite instead of CRA. The customize-cra and babel-plugin-module-resolver lessons become a few lines of resolve.alias in vite.config.js.
The video's libraries still install with React 19: axios, clsx, Font Awesome, Tippy. @tippyjs/react, though, has not been updated since 2022; see the note below.

items.label: ReactJS 2022
items.source: F8 Official · 83 videos, 27.5 h, TikTok project included

rows: SPA versus MPA, and an ES6 refresher: arrow functions, modules, spread, destructuring.
React elements, JSX, props, components. The Webpack and CRA setup (lessons 21–27) is replaced by the Vite section below.
Hooks: useState, useEffect, useRef, memo, useCallback, useMemo, useReducer, useContext.
CSS modules, clsx, SCSS, and React Router v6.
TikTok clone project: layouts, header, search calling an API with axios, sidebar.

sections.title: Create a project with Vite
sections.summary: Five minutes from the first command to React running in the browser.

items: Go to your code folder and run the create command below. Vite 8 needs Node 20.19 or 22.12+; part 1's Node 24 is enough.
Enter the project folder and run npm install to download the libraries into node_modules.
Run npm run dev and open localhost:5173. Change text in src/App.jsx and save: the page updates without losing state.
Stop the server with Ctrl + C. Commit the project to GitHub; node_modules is already in .gitignore.

body: Files containing JSX need the .jsx extension. The video uses .js for components, which Vite rejects with a syntax error, so rename files when copying.

sections.title: Components and JSX
sections.summary: One component taking props, one assembling a list.

blocks.caption: src/App.jsx: ProductCard takes props; App draws the list with map, each item with its own key.

items: className instead of class, htmlFor instead of for.
Braces {} insert any JavaScript expression: a variable, a calculation, a function call.
Every list item needs a stable key, usually an id. Avoid the array index when the list can be added to, removed from or sorted.
To return several sibling tags, wrap them in <>…</> (a Fragment).

sections.title: State and events
sections.summary: The to-do app rewritten in React: compare with part 3 to see the difference.

blocks.caption: The input is controlled by state; the list changes through new copies.
code: setTodos((prev) => [...prev, { id: crypto.randomUUID(), text, done: false }]);

items: Never mutate state: todos.push(x) changes nothing on screen; setTodos([...todos, x]) does.
When the new value comes from the old one, pass a function: setCount((c) => c + 1).
Events are camelCase and take a function: onClick={handleClick}, not onclick="handleClick()".

sections.title: useEffect and calling APIs
sections.summary: Three states every API screen has: loading, error, data.

blocks.caption: Fetch users from JSONPlaceholder, a free fake API for practice.

body: The function returned from useEffect is the cleanup. The ignore flag drops an old call's result when the component has left or rerun.

sections.title: Pages with React Router 8
sections.summary: Three files to touch, and the app has pages.

items: Install it: npm install react-router.
In src/main.jsx wrap App in BrowserRouter.
In App declare Routes: each Route ties a path to a component; path="*" catches everything else.
Use Link instead of an a tag to change pages without a reload; read URL parameters with useParams.

blocks.caption: src/App.jsx: three pages and a 404.
code: import { Link, Route, Routes, useParams } from 'react-router';

sections.title: Build the TikTok project with Vite
sections.summary: Replace the two CRA setup lessons (57–58) with these steps; follow the video for the rest.

items: Create the project with Vite as above, naming it tiktok-ui.
Install the libraries the video uses: the npm install line below.
Edit vite.config.js so ~ points at src, like the video's alias.
Create jsconfig.json so VS Code understands the ~ alias and completes paths.
From lesson 59 on, follow the video; remember .jsx for files with JSX.

blocks.caption: The libraries the TikTok project uses.
code: npm install react-router axios clsx @tippyjs/react tippy.js @fortawesome/react-fontawesome @fortawesome/fontawesome-svg-core @fortawesome/free-solid-svg-icons

blocks.caption: vite.config.js: the ~ alias points at src.

body: @tippyjs/react has not been updated since 2022. It still installs with React 19; if the console reports ref errors, build the dropdown in CSS or use @floating-ui/react instead.

sections.title: Tailwind CSS 4 (optional)
sections.summary: CSS written as utility classes; version 4 installs much more simply.

items: Install tailwindcss and its Vite plugin.
Add the tailwindcss() plugin to vite.config.js, next to react().
Replace src/index.css with the single line @import "tailwindcss".
Use classes in JSX, for example className="p-4 text-lg font-bold".

blocks.caption: src/index.css: one line is all it takes.

body: A video with tailwind.config.js and the three @tailwind base, components, utilities lines shows version 3's setup. Version 4 replaces it with the steps above; class names barely change.
